title: ReverseDock configuration (rdock.yaml)
description:
A complete ReverseDock configuration, as written in `rdock.yaml`.

Every section is optional. Names of listeners, routes, services, middlewares and
certificates are map keys; other objects refer to them by name.

$schema.description: JSON Schema reference for editors. Ignored by ReverseDock.

acme.description:
Automatic certificates (ACME). On by default with Let's Encrypt, HTTP-01 and TLS-ALPN-01;
`false` turns it off.

caches.description: HTTP cache stores, used by `cache` middlewares.

cluster.description:
Membership of a cluster (H-HA-01…03): the control plane this data plane takes its
configuration from, and where certificates are shared.

consumers.description:
API clients and users that requests are attributed to, with their API keys (stored
hashed). The `api` provider may add consumers and keys (`rdock consumers`).

control.description: The control plane's own settings, read only by `rdock control run`.

defaults.description: Defaults applied to routes that do not set a value.

experimental.description:
Experimental features this configuration uses on purpose (ADR-0033), e.g.
`[wasm, http3]`. A configuration that uses an experimental feature without naming it
here is refused: experimental features may change or be removed in any release and are
not covered by the stability promise.

geoip.description:
GeoIP databases for `ClientCountry`, `ClientContinent` and `ClientASN` (H-SEC-04). No
database is bundled or downloaded.

listeners.description:
Sockets to accept traffic on. When empty, `web` (`:80`) and `websecure` (`:443`, TLS)
are used.

locality.description: The proxy's own zone and whether services prefer backends in it (H-HA-05).

providers.description: Dynamic configuration sources (file, Docker, Swarm, Kubernetes).

routes.description: HTTP routes: which requests go to which service, through which middlewares.

runtime.description: The proxy's worker threads; read at start, so a change needs a restart.

secrets.description: External secret stores that secret fields can reference (`${vault:…}`).

security.description: Client IP trust and request limits.

services.description: Backend pools that routes send traffic to.

tcp_routes.description: TCP routes (SNI routing, passthrough, plain TCP).

tenants.description:
Tenants of the admin API (H-SEC-07): API tokens and users scoped to a tenant read and
write only the API objects under its name prefix, whose routes stay inside its host
claims. Without this section, nothing is scoped.

udp_routes.description: UDP routes: which `udp` listener's datagrams go to which UDP service.

upgrade.description:
In-place binary upgrades (`rdock upgrade`, `SIGUSR2`): the binary, the drain bound and
the start timeout.

version.description: Configuration format version. Only `1` exists; omit it to use the latest.

x-rdock-deprecations.note: The single v0.3 webhook has worked as a channel named `webhook` since v0.5. Its `timeout` has had no effect since then (channels wait 5 s), so it is dropped. A channel treats its `url` as a secret: write it as a `${file:…}` or `${env:…}` reference to avoid the warning.

Served; marked in the access log and for later middlewares.

redact.description: Header names whose values are replaced by `***`.

sample.description:
Share of successful requests (status below 400) that are logged, from 0 to 1. Errors
and failed requests are always logged.

ca.description: Certificate authority: a known name or an `https://` ACME directory URL.

ca_root.description:
PEM file with the root certificate of a CA whose ACME endpoint is not publicly trusted,
such as an internal step-ca. Only this root is then trusted for the CA's endpoint.

challenges.description: Challenge types to use, in order of preference.

dns_propagation_timeout.description: How long to wait for a DNS-01 record to become visible; the CA validates anyway after.

dns_provider.description:
DNS provider (a key of `dns_providers`) used for every route that does not name one:
all certificates are then validated with DNS-01.

dns_providers.description: DNS providers for DNS-01, referenced by routes.

dns_resolvers.description:
Resolvers (`ip` or `ip:port`) that must see a DNS-01 record before the CA is asked to
validate. By default the zone's authoritative nameservers are asked.

eab.description: External account binding, required by some CAs.

email.description: Contact address for the CA account (optional for Let's Encrypt).

profile.description:
Certificate profile (Let's Encrypt): `classic` (90 days), `tlsserver` (45 days) or
`shortlived` (about 6 days, needed for IP addresses).

staging.description: Use the CA's staging environment (untrusted certificates, high rate limits).

storage.description: Where accounts and certificates are stored. Defaults to `$RDOCK_DATA_DIR/acme`.

oneOf.description: 90-day certificates (the default).
45-day certificates without legacy fields.
About 6-day certificates; the only profile that allows IP addresses.

AcmeSetting.description: The `acme` section: `false` turns automatic certificates off, `true` or settings keep them on.

anyOf.description: `true` uses the defaults; `false` turns automatic certificates off.

expected_body.description: Text the response body must contain (HTTP).

grpc_service.description: gRPC service name to check; empty checks the whole server.

healthy.description: Consecutive successes before a backend is healthy.

hostname.description: `Host` of the probe (HTTP); the backend address when unset.

port.description: Probe this port instead of the backend's.

unhealthy.description: Consecutive failures before a backend is unhealthy.

allowed_hosts.description:
Host names the admin listener answers to; other `Host` headers get 421 (DNS-rebinding
defence). Default: `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `::1` on loopback, the listener's IP
otherwise. Required when `listener` is on all interfaces.

api_writes.description:
Allow configuration changes through the admin API and the dashboard. Set `false`
(`GitOps`) when Git and the file provider are the only source of truth.

dashboard.description: Serve the embedded dashboard on the admin listener.

listener.description: Address of the admin API. Loopback by default; any other address needs `tls`.

metrics_unauthenticated_on_loopback.description:
Serve `/metrics` without a token when the listener is a loopback address, as before
v0.5, for scrapers on the same machine that cannot send one.

mfa.description: Who must use a second factor (TOTP) to log in.

sessions.description: How long a dashboard login lasts.

socket.description:
Unix socket for the local CLI (`rdock reload`, `rdock status`), mode 0600. Default:
`$RDOCK_DATA_DIR/admin.sock`.

threads.description: Worker threads of the admin runtime, kept apart from the proxy's (1–16).

tls.description: TLS for the admin listener. Required when `listener` is not a loopback address.

tokens.description: API tokens for scripts and Prometheus.

trust_forwarded_on_loopback.description:
Take the client's address from `X-Forwarded-For` on connections from loopback. Turn it
on only when a route of this rdock forwards to the admin listener, so rate limits and
token networks see real clients; any local process could otherwise claim an address.

AdminAudit.description:
The audit log (ADR-0024): every admin write, login, MFA event, refusal and session end, as
JSON lines that each carry the SHA-256 of the line before.

forward.description: Also send each record to a syslog server.

max_file_size.description: A file is closed and a new one started at this size (1 MiB–1 GiB).

retention.description: How long rotated files are kept (1d–3650d).

AdminPasswords.description:
Password rules for dashboard users (ADR-0024). There are no composition rules: length and
a list of common passwords are what protect a password (NIST SP 800-63B §3.1.1.2).

argon2.description:
Argon2id cost. Values below the OWASP minimum are refused; existing hashes are
upgraded at the next login after a change.

blocklist_file.description:
A file with one password per line (for example a breached-password list) refused in
addition to the bundled list of common passwords. Read once at start, offline.

min_length.description: Shortest password accepted, in characters (8–128). The longest is 128.

AdminSessions.description:
Dashboard session lifetimes (ADR-0024; OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet, checked
2026-10-31). Both are between 5 minutes and 12 hours.

absolute.description: A session ends this long after login, however active.

idle.description: A session without requests for this long ends.

AdminTls.description: Certificate and key the admin listener presents.

allow_no_expiry.description: Allow tokens that never expire. Off by default: a leaked token should stop working.

default_expiry_days.description: Lifetime of a new token when its creator gives none, in days (1–365).

oneOf.description: Additive increase, multiplicative decrease on slow or failed samples.
The measured no-load latency against each sample's (Envoy's gradient).

AdmissionShares.description: How much of the limit each lower priority class may fill.

normal.description: Routes with `priority_class: normal`, in percent of the limit (default 90).

sheddable.description:
Routes with `priority_class: sheddable`, in percent of the limit (default 75; at most
`normal`).

AgentBreaker.description:
An agent's circuit breaker: after `failures` failed calls in a row, the most recent within
`window` of the first, the agent is not called for `open_for`; `on_error` applies at once
meanwhile. Then one call is tried: success closes the breaker, failure opens it again.

failures.description: Failed calls in a row that open the breaker; `0` turns it off.

open_for.description: How long the breaker stays open.

window.description: The failures must fall within this time.

AgentOnError.description: What an agent failure does to the request.

oneOf.description: Refuse the request (fail closed).
Let the request through unchecked (fail open); counted and logged.

AgentOversize.description: What a body longer than `max_body` does.

oneOf.description: Refuse the request with `413`.
Ask the agent without the body.

ApiKeyEntry.description:
One API key of a consumer: `rdk_<id>_<secret><checksum>` is the key, and only `id` and the
SHA-256 of the secret are stored.

expires.description: When the key stops working: an RFC 3339 time, e.g. `2027-01-01T00:00:00Z`.

hash.description:
SHA-256 of the key's secret (the 32 characters after the ID's `_`, without the
6-character checksum), as 64 lower-case hex digits. `rdock keys hash` prints it.

Argon2id parameters. The default is the OWASP minimum, m=19456 KiB, t=2, p=1 (Password

Syslog server as `host:port`; records are RFC 5424 messages with the JSON record as

`udp` (default), `tcp` (octet counting, RFC 6587) or `tls` (RFC 5425). Only `tls`

Azure DNS (`type: azure_dns`). Exactly one of `client_secret`, `client_certificate` and
`managed_identity` is set.

Authenticate as the managed identity of the Azure VM or service ReverseDock runs on,

for_zones.description:

Priority tier from 0 (the default, used first) to 7. See the service's `failover`.
Not together with `backup`.

patch.description:
A JSON Patch (RFC 6902): operations `add`, `remove`, `replace`, `move`, `copy` and
`test` with JSON Pointers (RFC 6901), applied in order, all or nothing.

ByteSize.description: Size in bytes, optionally with a unit (KB = 1000, KiB = 1024).

A cache store: where cached responses live. Stores are created once per process; adding
one applies on reload, changing or removing one takes effect after a restart.

max_size.description: Bytes kept, bodies and headers together.

Responses on disk, one file per object, evicted least recently used first beyond
`max_size` or `max_objects`. Objects survive restarts.

max_objects.description: Objects kept on disk (one file each).

path.description:
Directory of the store, absolute; `<data dir>/cache/<name>` when omitted. Created with
mode 0700. Anyone who can write it can serve arbitrary content through the cache.

A certificate and private key provided as files. Changes to the files are picked up
automatically.

Password of an encrypted key. Reference a secret instead of writing it here:
`"${file:/run/secrets/key_password}"`.

How a client certificate is passed to the backend. Copies of these headers sent by clients

Cluster.description: The data-plane side of a cluster.

control.description: The control plane this data plane takes its configuration from.

instance.description:
This instance's name in leases and the control plane's instance list: letters, digits,
`.`, `-` and `_`, at most 63 characters. Default: the identity the control plane gave
at enrolment, or (without a control plane) an id generated once and kept in
`$RDOCK_DATA_DIR/cluster/instance`.

limits.description: How `rate_limit` and `quota` with `scope: cluster` share their budgets.

store.description:
Where certificates, the ACME account, leases and challenge answers are shared. Default:
the control plane when `control` is set.

ClusterControl.description: How a data plane reaches its control plane.

ca_file.description:
The cluster CA certificate (PEM), as `rdock control ca` prints it. One of `ca_file` and
`ca_pin` is required.

ca_pin.description:
The SHA-256 of the cluster CA certificate (DER), as `sha256:<64 hex digits>`; `rdock
control token create` prints it. The first connection accepts the control plane only
when its chain contains a CA with this digest; the CA is then kept in `identity_dir`.

identity_dir.description:
Where the instance's key, certificate and the cluster CA are kept (mode 0700). Default
`$RDOCK_DATA_DIR/cluster`.

join_token.description:
The single-use join token from `rdock control token create`, used only while the
instance has no identity yet. A secret: reference a file, e.g.
`"${file:/run/secrets/rdock-join}"`.

poll_timeout.description:
How long one request for the next bundle waits on the control plane before it is asked
again. Default 30s (5s–5m).

url.description:
The control plane's cluster address, e.g. `https://control.example.com:7443`. Always
`https`.

ClusterLimits.description:
Shared budgets for `rate_limit` and `quota` with `scope: cluster` (ADR-0031).

Each instance claims a part of each key's budget from the store ahead of use and admits
requests against what it claimed, so the request path never waits on the store. The
cluster admits at most `L + N × max(c, ⌈L / N⌉)` per key and window, where `L` is the
limit, `N` the number of instances, `c = max(1, ⌈L × headroom_percent / (100 × N)⌉)` the
headroom an instance may use beyond its claims, and `⌈L / N⌉` what an instance admits for a
key new to it until its first claim returns.

fallback.description: `share` (default) or `instance`: what an instance enforces while the store is away.

headroom_percent.description:
How far an instance may admit beyond the budget it has claimed, as a percentage of the
limit split between the instances: larger values absorb store latency at high request
rates, smaller ones tighten the bound. Default 10 (0–100).

sync_interval.description:
How often claims, membership and recovery are attended to (claims a request needs are
sent at once). Default 1s (100ms–10s).

ClusterStore.description: Where a cluster shares certificates, the ACME account, leases and challenge answers.

barrier_timeout.description:
How long the instance that orders a certificate waits for every live member to hold an
HTTP-01 or TLS-ALPN-01 answer before the CA is told to validate. Members that have not
confirmed by then cannot answer; validation goes ahead. Default 10s (1s–2m).

lease_ttl.description:
How long a lease on a certificate name lasts unless its holder renews it (every third of
it). Default 60s (10s–10m).

oneOf.description:
The control plane serves the store to enrolled members over mutual TLS. Leases carry a
fencing token the control plane checks on every write.

A directory every instance mounts (NFS, EFS, a shared volume). Best effort: lock files
with an expiry that depends on the instances' clocks, and no enforced fencing.
gzip.
Brotli.
Zstandard.

Consumer.description:
A consumer: an API client or user that requests are attributed to (`consumers.<name>`).

An authenticating middleware (`api_key`, `oidc`, `cloudflare_access`, `jwt` with
`consumer_claim`) sets the request's consumer;
rate limits and quotas can count per consumer, and the access log, metrics, metering and the
cache key see its name.

groups.description:
Groups, in order of precedence: per-group limit overrides use the first listed group
that has one, and `api_key.groups` admits a consumer in any of them. In the admin
API's document, an entry without `groups` only adds keys to a consumer of the file.

keys.description: API keys, stored as their ID and the SHA-256 of their secret; never the key itself.

keys_file.description:
A file of `id:sha256[:expires]` lines (blank lines and `#` comments ignored), read on
every reload and watched like the configuration file.

ControlPlane.description: The control-plane side of a cluster, read by `rdock control run` (never by `rdock run`).

history.description: Published revisions kept for listing and rollback. Default 50 (1–1000).

identity_lifetime.description:
Lifetime of the client certificate each data plane receives; it is renewed when a third
is left. A data plane whose certificate expires while the control plane is away keeps
serving but must enrol again with a new token. Default 30d (1h–90d).

join_token_ttl.description:
How long a join token from `rdock control token create` stays usable. Default 1h
(1m–30d).

listener.description:
The cluster listener data planes connect to (mutual TLS, HTTP/2). Default
`127.0.0.1:7443`: set an address other machines reach.

name.description: A display name for the cluster.

names.description:
DNS names and IP addresses on the control plane's server certificate, as data planes
write them in `cluster.control.url`. `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1` and the listener's
IP are always included.

offline_after.description:
A data plane that has not asked for a bundle for this long is shown as offline and is
not chosen as a canary. Default 90s (10s–1h).

rollout.description: How a published revision reaches the data planes: one canary first, then the rest.

certificate.description:
Certificate (a key of `certificates`) served when no other certificate matches the
requested name, or when the client sends no name (SNI).

errors.description:
How answers rdock produces itself (404 without a route, 401/403/429 from middlewares,
502/503/504) are rendered, for routes that do not set `errors`.

listeners.description: Listeners used by routes that do not name any.

redirect_http_to_https.description: Redirect plain HTTP requests to HTTPS for hosts that have a TLS route.

tls.description: TLS for routes that do not set `tls`: `auto` (automatic certificates) or `off`.

api_url.description: For tests only: another API base URL, `http://` only on a loopback address.

token.description:
API token; a token policy can limit it to writing the `_acme-challenge` TXT RRsets of one

body a client may send before rdock reads it. Default 65535 bytes (the protocol's
initial value); at most 2^31-1.

Streams a client may have open at once (`SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS`). Default 100
(Pingora's bound); at most 10000 unless `unlimited`.

max_frame_size.description:
Largest frame payload rdock accepts (`SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE`). Default 16384; 16384
to 16777215 (RFC 9113 §6.5.2).

max_header_list_size.description:
Largest decoded request header list (`SETTINGS_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE`). Default 64KiB
(Pingora's bound); 1KiB to 16MiB.

Streams rdock resets because the client misbehaved before the connection is closed (the
`MadeYouReset` mitigation, CVE-2025-8671). Default 1024 (h2's); at most 100000 unless
`unlimited`.

Streams a client may reset before rdock accepted them, at once (the HTTP/2 Rapid Reset
mitigation, CVE-2023-44487). Default 20 (h2's); at most 10000 unless `unlimited`.

unlimited.

Add `Alt-Svc: h3=":<port>"` to this listener's HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 responses while the
QUIC endpoint serves (RFC 9114 §3.1.1). Default `true`.

is 24h; shorter while experimental); 1s to 30d.

public 443 to container 8443). Default: the listener's port.

extended_connect.description:

(planned).

(`initial_max_streams_bidi`). Default 100; 1 to 10000.

memory is `max_connections × (2 × receive_window + send_window)`: about 3 GiB with the

prefix of `client_ipv6_prefix` bits. Only connections whose address is validated count.

Largest request header section (`SETTINGS_MAX_FIELD_SECTION_SIZE`, counted as RFC 9114
§4.2.2 does: name + value + 32 bytes per field). Default 64KiB; 1KiB to 768KiB, and at
most `receive_window`.

Close a connection with no activity for this long (QUIC `max_idle_timeout`). Default
30s (HAProxy's); 1s to 10m.

Let clients move a connection to another address (active migration). Not supported
(planned). With migration off, quinn 0.11 drops packets from a new address, so a client

`initial_max_data`). rdock also holds at most this much of incomplete HEADERS and other
non-DATA frames per connection. Default 1MiB; 64KiB to 64MiB.

(RFC 9000 §8.1.2). `auto` (default) sends Retry while 100 or more connections are

threshold only. Whatever the setting, a client whose address is not yet validated is
sent Retry instead of being refused when the listener is full, when its address already

connections reach half of `max_connections`: spoofed packets can neither lock a client

allow_private_targets.description: Allow a receiver on a private, loopback or link-local address.

secret.description:
A Standard Webhooks signing secret (`whsec_…`) as a `${file:…}` or `${env:…}`
reference: requests carry `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` and `webhook-signature`.

token.description: A bearer token as a `${file:…}` or `${env:…}` reference.

prometheus.description: Serve Prometheus metrics at `/metrics` on the admin listener.

MfaPolicy.description: Who must log in with a TOTP code besides the password.

oneOf.description: Admins must enrol before they can do anything else; others may.
Every user must enrol.
Nobody must; anyone may.

Middleware.description: A reusable request/response policy, selected by `type`.

oneOf.description: Set, add or remove request and response headers.

hsts.description: HTTP Strict Transport Security, sent on HTTPS responses only.

request.description: Changes to the request sent to the backend.

response.description: Changes to the response sent to the client.

oneOf.description: Redirect to another scheme or to a URL built from a regular expression.

always.description:
Redirect even a request that already uses `scheme` (a redirect that sets `hostname`,
`path` or `prefix` is always sent). The Gateway API's `RequestRedirect` filter sets it:
there a redirect is sent whatever the request's scheme. Default `false`.

permanent.description:
`301`/`308` when true, `302`/`307` when false (the second code of each pair is used for
methods other than GET, so the method and body are kept), as in Traefik.

port.description:
Port of the target, left out of the URL when it is the scheme's default. Unset: the
scheme's default port when `scheme` is set, otherwise the request's port.

prefix.description:
Replace a leading path prefix, by path segment: `{ from: /a, to: /b }` turns `/a/x`
into `/b/x` and `/a` into `/b`; other paths are kept.

regex.description:
Regular expression matched against the full request URL. Not combined with the
fields above.

replacement.description: Target URL; may use `$1`, `${name}` groups from `regex`.

scheme.description:
Redirect to this scheme. Alone (without `hostname`, `path` or `prefix`; `port`,
`status` and `permanent` may be set), a request that already uses it is not
redirected, unless `always` is set.

status.description:
Status code of the redirect: `301`, `302`, `303`, `307` or `308`, for every method.
Overrides `permanent`.

oneOf.description: Rewrite the path with a regular expression.

regex.description: Regular expression matched against the path.

oneOf.description: Remove a path prefix before forwarding.

prefixes.description: Prefixes to remove; the first that matches is used.

oneOf.description: Add a path prefix before forwarding.
Replace the whole path before forwarding.
HTTP Basic authentication with hashed passwords.

users_file.description: File with one `user:hash` entry per line.

oneOf.description: Ask an external service (Authelia, Authentik, oauth2-proxy…) whether to allow a request.

address.description:
Authentication endpoint. A 2xx answer allows the request; anything else is returned to
the client.

copy_headers.description: Response headers of the auth service copied to the forwarded request.

request_headers.description: Request headers sent to the auth service (all when empty).

timeout.description: Time allowed for the auth service. Requests fail closed on timeout.

trust_forward_header.description: Trust `X-Forwarded-*` headers already present on the request.

oneOf.description: Allow only these client networks.
Reject these client networks.
Token-bucket rate limiting.

headers.description:
`draft` adds `RateLimit-Policy` and `RateLimit` to responses
(`draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-11`). Off by default.

overrides.description:
Group → limit for consumers in that group, with `key: consumer` or `key: group`. With
`consumer`, the first of the consumer's groups (in its `groups` order) that has an
override wins; with `group`, the override of the primary group (the first one) applies.

scope.description:
`instance` (default) or `cluster`. With `cluster`, the cluster admits at most
`average` requests per key in each `period` (fixed windows from the Unix epoch), within
the bound of `cluster.limits`; each instance's own token bucket still shapes bursts.

oneOf.description: A cap on requests in flight, with an optional queue (Traefik's `inFlightReq`).

amount.description: Requests in flight allowed per key.

queue.description: Requests over the limit that wait for a slot; more get `429` at once.

queue_timeout.description: How long a queued request waits before it gets `429`.

scope.description: Only `instance`: a cluster-wide count of requests in flight is planned.

oneOf.description: A cap on response bytes per second.

burst.description: Bytes that may be sent at once before the rate applies; defaults to `rate`.

oneOf.description: Cross-origin resource sharing.

allow_credentials.description: Allow cookies and credentials. Not allowed together with `*`.

max_age.description: How long browsers may cache the preflight answer.

oneOf.description: Response compression.

algorithms.description: Algorithms offered, in order of preference.

content_types.description: Content types to compress; common text types when empty.

oneOf.description: Custom error pages.

file.description: Static HTML file to serve. Set this or `service`.

path.description: Path requested from `service`; `{status}` is replaced by the code.

service.description: Service that renders the error page. Set this or `file`.

status.description: Status codes or ranges, e.g. `404` or `500-599`.

oneOf.description: Maintenance mode.

allow.description: Clients that still reach the service (e.g. your office).

oneOf.description: Verify JSON Web Tokens (JWS) and pass their claims on.

algorithms.description: Algorithms accepted. `none` does not exist here.

audiences.description: Accepted `aud` values (one must match); `[any]` accepts every audience.

claims_to_headers.description: Request headers set from claims (`claim: header`). Client-sent copies are removed first.

consumer_claim.description:
A claim that becomes the request's consumer (for `rate_limit` and `quota` with
`key: consumer`, the cache key and the access log), e.g. `sub` or `email`.

forward_token.description: Keep the token in the request to the backend.

groups_claim.description:
The claim listing the consumer's groups (a string or an array of strings), with
`consumer_claim`.

hmac_secret.description: Shared secret for HS256/HS384/HS512 tokens, as a `${file:…}` or `${env:…}` reference.

jwks_file.description: A JSON Web Key Set file, read on every reload.

jwks_url.description: URL of a JSON Web Key Set, fetched in the background and cached for 10 minutes.

map_to_consumers.description:
With `consumer_claim`: treat a name that `consumers` defines as that consumer, adding
its groups and sharing its quota, rate-limit and cache identity with its API keys
(other names stay keyed on the issuer). Off by default: a token's consumer is a
separate identity keyed on the token's issuer and the name. Turn it on only when the
issuer controls the claim.

token.description: Where the token is read from; `Authorization: Bearer` when empty.

trusted_groups.description:
Groups from `groups_claim` that count for `key: group` and for group `overrides` of
`rate_limit` and `quota`, as if configured. Other token groups are kept on the
consumer (metering, headers) but never share a configured group's budget or override,
and a consumer with only those is counted on its own.

unverified_emails.description:
With `consumer_claim: email`: accept an `email` claim that comes without
`email_verified`. Off: the address names the consumer only with `email_verified:
true`, otherwise `sub` does (`email_verified: false` never counts). Unsafe with an
issuer that lets users set an address they do not own.

oneOf.description: Demand a verified client certificate, check its names and pass its identity on.

allow.description:
Names a certificate must have one of: its common name or a DNS, URI or email SAN.
`*` matches any run of characters, e.g. `*.clients.example.com`. Any name when empty.
The typed lists below check one field each and are safer: a URI pattern there cannot
be satisfied by a common name that carries the same text.

dns.description: DNS SANs, one must match (`*` globs).

emails.description: Email SANs, one must match (`*` globs).

forward.description: Headers that pass the identity to the backend.

organizations.description: Subject organizations (O), one must match (`*` globs).

required.description: Answer `403` to requests without a verified client certificate.

serials.description: Certificate serial numbers in hex (`0a1b…`, colons allowed), exact.

sha256.description: SHA-256 fingerprints of the certificate in hex (colons allowed), exact: pins.

spiffe.description:
SPIFFE X.509-SVID rules (H-SEC-05): the certificate must be a valid SVID of one of the
trust domains, and its ID one of `ids` or under one of `id_prefixes`.

subjects.description:
Subject common names, one must match (`*` globs). Every typed list that is set must
match, together with `allow`.

uris.description: URI SANs, one must match (`*` globs).

oneOf.description:
Translate gRPC-Web from browsers into gRPC for the backend (binary
`application/grpc-web`; the service needs `scheme: h2c` or `https`).

Serve files from a directory on ReverseDock's own file system. It answers the request,
so a route that ends with it needs no service (unless `pass_through` is on).

directory_redirect.description:
Redirect (`308`) a directory path without a trailing slash to the path with one when the
directory has an index file, or is listed.

fallback.description:
File served (with status 200) for a GET or HEAD whose last path segment has no `.` and
that names no file, e.g. `/index.html` for a single-page app. Off when unset.

fallback_except.description: Path prefixes that never get the `fallback`, e.g. `/api/`; they stay `404`.

hidden.description: Files and directories whose name starts with `.` (`.env`, `.git/`).

index.description: File names tried, in order, for a request that names a directory.

listing.description:
List a directory that has no `index` file (F-WEB-02): HTML, or JSON for clients that
prefer it in `Accept`. Off by default. Follows `hidden` and `symlinks`: names a request
would be refused are not listed. At most 10,000 entries, sorted by name. A directory
that exists is listed instead of getting the `fallback`.

max_ranges.description:
Most byte ranges answered in one request, from 1 to 16. A request for more gets the
whole file (`200`); more than 1 allows `multipart/byteranges` answers.

pass_through.description:
Send requests that name no file (and methods other than GET and HEAD) on to the route's
service instead of answering `404` or `405`. The route then needs a service.

precompressed.description:
Precompressed sidecar files (`app.js.zst`, `app.js.br`, `app.js.gz`) served to clients
that accept the coding, in this order of preference. `[]` turns them off.

root.description: Directory to serve. It must exist and be a directory when the configuration is applied.

types.description: File extension → media type, overriding the built-in table, e.g. `{ ts: text/typescript }`.

oneOf.description:
Hold the request body until it is complete (up to `max`) before any of it reaches the
backend. The backend connection and the request head are already sent, so this does
not shield backend workers from slow uploads; it refuses oversize bodies with `413`
and lets body middlewares see the whole body.

max.description:
Largest body held, at most 64MiB; a longer one is refused with `413`. The route's
`max_body` (or `security.limits.max_body_bytes`) applies when it is smaller.

timeout.description:
Longest time from the first body byte to the last; a slower upload is refused with
`408`. The service's `timeouts.read` also runs while the backend waits for the body.

oneOf.description:
Cache responses in a store named under `caches` (RFC 9111). Only what the origin's
headers allow is stored; see `docs/guides/caching`.

authorization.description:
Responses to requests that carry `Authorization` to the origin: `refuse` (default)
stores them only when they are marked `public`, `s-maxage` or `must-revalidate` (RFC
9111 §3.5); `store` stores them anyway. The risk of `store` is serving one
credential's answer to another.

background_refresh.description:
Refresh stale responses in the background (`stale-while-revalidate`). Not supported
in this version: `stale-while-revalidate` is treated as plain staleness.

bypass.description: Requests that skip the cache entirely.

cookies.description: Skip when the request has one of these cookies.

headers.description: Skip when the request has one of these headers.

default_ttl.description:
Lifetime by status (`"200": 5m`) for responses whose origin gives none (no
`max-age`, `s-maxage` or `Expires`). Never applies over `no-store`, `private` or
`no-cache`. Empty by default: the risk is caching personalised pages the origin did
not mark.

heuristic_freshness.description:
Give responses with `Last-Modified` and no explicit lifetime 10 % of their age, at
most a day (RFC 9111 §4.2.2). Off by default: the origin did not ask for caching.

key.description: What, besides store, route, scheme, host, path and method, selects a stored response.

consumer.description:
Keep one copy per authenticated identity: the consumer, else the `basic_auth` user,
else the `jwt` issuer and subject, else the client certificate's subject.

headers.description: Request headers whose values select a response (beyond the origin's `Vary`).

query.description: How the query string enters the key.

lock.description: Request coalescing: one origin fetch per key at a time.

enabled.description:
While one request fetches a key, others wait for its response instead of asking the
origin too. Off, every miss goes to the origin.

timeout.description:
Longest wait. After it the waiting request goes to the origin without storing, and
a fetch running that long no longer holds others back.

max_object_size.description: Largest response body stored; larger ones pass through uncached.

remove_targeted.description:
Remove the targeted fields from responses to clients (RFC 9213 §2.2 allows it). Off
by default: a CDN in front of this proxy needs `CDN-Cache-Control` too, and without
it would fall back to the less specific `Cache-Control`.

request_directives.description:
The client's `no-cache`, `max-age`, `min-fresh` and `max-stale`: `honour` (default,
RFC 9111 §5.2.1) or `ignore`, so clients cannot force origin fetches.
`only-if-cached` is always honoured.

set_cookie.description:
Responses that set a cookie: `refuse` (default) never stores them; `strip` stores
them without `Set-Cookie`. The risk of `strip` is a page that depends on the cookie.

shared_across_users.description:
The route authenticates requests but its responses are the same for every user, so
one stored copy may be served to all of them. Required (or `key.consumer`) when the
route has an authenticating middleware; the risk is serving one user's page to
another.

stale_if_error.description:
Longest time a stale response is served when the origin fails, if the origin allowed
it with `stale-if-error` (RFC 5861). `0s` turns it off.

statuses.description:
Statuses that may be stored, each only with a lifetime; default 200, 203, 204, 300,
301, 308, 404, 410. 206 and 304 are never stored as such.

tags.description: Cache tags for purging groups of responses.

headers.description: Response headers that carry tags (comma or space separated).

keep.description: Pass the tag headers on to clients; by default they are removed.

targeted.description:
Targeted cache-control fields honoured, in order (RFC 9213): the first one with a
valid, non-empty value replaces `Cache-Control` and `Expires` for this cache, in both
directions (`CDN-Cache-Control: no-store` keeps a fresh response out; `max-age=600`
stores one marked `Cache-Control: no-store`). Default `[CDN-Cache-Control]`: from the
origin's side this cache is the CDN tier. `[]` reads `Cache-Control` only; a name of
your own first (`[RDock-Cache-Control, CDN-Cache-Control]`) targets this cache alone.

oneOf.description:
A native plugin compiled into this binary and registered under `name` (ADR-0030). The
stock `rdock` binary registers none; see `docs/guides/plugins`.

config.description:
The plugin's own settings, checked by the plugin when the configuration is validated
and loaded. Values are interpolated like any other (`${env:…}`, `${file:…}`) and stay
visible in the configuration API.

name.description: The name the plugin is registered under in this binary.

oneOf.description:
A sandboxed WebAssembly plugin (ADR-0030): a component for the world
`rdock:plugin/filter@0.1.0`, loaded from a file pinned by SHA-256 and signed with
minisign. Experimental: name `wasm` under `experimental`. Needs a build with the `wasm`
cargo feature; see `docs/guides/wasm-plugins`.

allow_unsigned.description:
UNSAFE: run the module without a signature (the `sha256` pin still applies). A
signature that is present must still verify. Logged as a warning at every load.

capabilities.description:
Host interfaces the plugin may import besides its `config`. A component that imports
one not listed here, or anything else (WASI included), is refused when it is loaded.

config.description: The plugin's own settings, given to it as JSON text through `rdock:plugin/config`.

fuel.description: Fuel per call, about one unit per WebAssembly instruction; a call that runs out fails.

memory.description: The largest linear memory the plugin may have.

on_error.description:
What a failed call (fuel, timeout, memory, trap, an invalid result) does: `deny`
answers `500` (in the response phase, the response is replaced by a `500`), `allow`
passes the request or response on unchanged. Both are counted and logged.

path.description:
The component file (`.wasm`; `.wat` text is accepted too). Read when the configuration
is loaded; a reload reads it again.

sha256.description:
The file's SHA-256 digest, 64 hex digits (`sha256sum plugin.wasm`). Required: it
fixes which file runs, so a changed file is refused until the pin is updated.

signature.description:
The minisign signature file; default `<path>.minisig` (what `minisign -S -m <path>`
writes).

timeout.description:
Wall-clock time allowed per call (a backstop to `fuel`; resolution about 1 ms). The
call runs on a proxy worker thread, so keep it short.

trusted_keys.description:
Minisign public keys whose signatures are accepted: the base64 line of a `.pub` file
(`RWQ…`).

oneOf.description:
Ask an out-of-process agent (a WAF, a policy service) whether to allow a request,
with its body up to `max_body` (ADR-0030). Fails closed by default.

address.description:
The agent's URL (`http://` or `https://`). Use `https://` or a loopback address unless
the network between rdock and the agent is private.

breaker.description: The circuit breaker that stops calling a failing agent for a while.

max_body.description:
Largest request body sent to the agent; `0` sends none. The body is held until the
agent has answered, so none of the body reaches the backend before the verdict; the
request head does: with a body, the backend connection is opened and the head sent
before the body is read (Pingora 0.9.1), and a refusal closes that connection.

on_error.description:
What happens when the agent cannot answer (unreachable, timeout, an invalid answer, an
open breaker): `deny` refuses the request (502, 504 on timeout, 503 while the breaker
is open), `allow` lets it through unchecked.

on_oversize.description:
A body longer than `max_body`: `reject` answers `413`, `skip` asks the agent without
the body (only when the length is declared; a chunked body that grows past
`max_body` is refused with `413` either way).

protocol.description: How the request is described to the agent.

request_headers.description:
Request headers sent to the agent besides the default set (`accept`,
`accept-encoding`, `accept-language`, `cache-control`, `content-type`, `origin`,
`referer`, `user-agent`); `["*"]` sends every header except hop-by-hop ones.
`authorization`, `cookie` and `proxy-authorization` go only when listed here.

response_headers.description:
Request headers the agent may set on the request that goes to the backend (allowed
answers only). Copies sent by the client are removed first. Applied only when the
verdict comes before the request head leaves, which is the case for requests without
a body (or whose body is not sent to the agent).

timeout.description: Time allowed for the agent's whole answer.

oneOf.description:
Verify the token Cloudflare Access adds to requests it let through (W-CF-06): a preset
over `jwt` with the team's keys, issuer and RS256, the token from the
`Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion` header, then the `CF_Authorization` cookie.

audience.description:
The Application Audience (AUD) tag of the Access application, or several. Required:
without it a token of any application of the same team would pass.

certs_url.description:
Where the keys are fetched from instead of the team's certs URL: for tests, or an
egress proxy that mirrors it. `https://` (or a loopback address).

claims_to_headers.description:
Request headers set from claims (`claim: header`), e.g. `{ email: X-Auth-Email,
common_name: X-Auth-Service-Token }`. Client-sent copies are removed first.

team.description: The Zero Trust team name (`acme`) or team domain (`acme.cloudflareaccess.com`).

oneOf.description:
Authenticate with consumers' API keys (`rdk_…`), read from `Authorization: Bearer` or
`X-API-Key`; sets the request's consumer (F-GW-01).

anonymous.description:
Requests without a key: `deny` answers `401`; `allow` lets them through without a
consumer (an invalid key is still refused).

forward_credential.description:
Keep the key in the request to the backend. Off by default: the backend gets the
consumer in `X-Consumer-Name`, `X-Consumer-Groups` and `X-Credential-Id` instead.

groups.description:
Only consumers in one of these groups are let in; others get `403`. Any consumer when
empty.

headers.description:
Request headers the key is read from, in order; the first present wins. A key in
`Authorization` must follow `Bearer `.

query.description:
A query parameter the key is also read from, after the headers. Off unless named: keys
in URLs end up in other systems' logs.

oneOf.description:
Requests per consumer per calendar window (hour, day, month), persisted across
restarts; `429` when used up (F-GW-02).

flush_interval.description: How often counters are written to disk.

headers.description:
`draft` adds `RateLimit-Policy` and `RateLimit` to responses, in the syntax of
`draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-11`. Off by default while the draft changes.

key.description:
What to count by: `consumer` (the default) or `group` (the consumer's primary group,
the first of its `groups`: all consumers of a group share one count). Requests without
a consumer are counted per client IP.

overrides.description:
Group → limit, for consumers in that group (with `key: consumer`, the first of the
consumer's groups that has one wins; with `key: group`, the primary group's).

scope.description:
`instance` (default) or `cluster`: with `cluster`, the instances of a cluster share each
key's quota through `cluster.limits`, within its documented bound.

window.description: The calendar window, in UTC: `hour`, `day` (from 00:00) or `month` (from the 1st).

oneOf.description:
Check request parameters and JSON bodies against JSON Schema 2020-12, inline or from an
OpenAPI 3.1 document; `400` with the errors when they do not match (F-GW-03).

base_path.description:
With `openapi`: a prefix the document's paths are relative to (`/api` when the
document's server URL is `https://example.com/api`). Requests outside it are unknown
operations.

body.description:
A schema for the JSON request body. A body with another content type is answered
`415`, a body that is not JSON `400`, a body over `max_body` `413`.

body_required.description:
With `body`: a request without a body is refused. Off by default, as OpenAPI's
`requestBody.required`.

cookies.description: A schema for the object of request cookies. Converted like `query`.

formats.description:
Check `format` (`date-time`, `email`, `uuid`, …) as an assertion. JSON Schema 2020-12
treats it as an annotation unless asked; rdock asks by default.

headers.description:
A schema for the object of request headers, keyed by lower-case name. Converted like
`query`.

max_body.description:
Largest body checked, at most 64MiB; the body is held until it is complete. The
route's `max_body` applies when it is smaller.

max_errors.description: Most errors listed in an answer (1 to 100).

mode.description:
`enforce` (the default) refuses invalid requests; `report` only logs and counts them,
to try a schema on live traffic.

openapi.description:
An OpenAPI 3.1 document (JSON or YAML), read on every reload. Requests are matched to
its operations by method and path template; each operation's parameters and its
`application/json` request body are checked.

path.description:
Path parameters: a regular expression for the path with named groups, and a schema for
the object of the groups' values.

query.description:
A schema for the object of query parameters (`{ name: value }`; a repeated name gives
an array). Values are strings, converted to the `type` the schema declares for the
property (`integer`, `number`, `boolean`, `array`).

unknown_operations.description:
With `openapi`: requests that match no operation of the document. `deny` (the
default) answers `404` or `405`; `allow` lets them through unchecked.

oneOf.description:
Change request and response headers, and JSON bodies with JSON Patch (RFC 6902)
(F-GW-04).

max_body.description:
Largest body patched, request or response, at most 64MiB (default 1MiB). A larger
request body is refused with `413`; a larger response body passes unchanged.

on_error.description:
A request patch that cannot be applied (a `test` operation fails, a location is
missing): `reject` (the default) answers `422`; `pass` forwards the body unchanged.
A response patch that fails always leaves the body unchanged (the status is sent).

on_non_json.description:
A request body that is not JSON when `request.body.patch` is set: `pass` (the
default) forwards it unchanged; `reject` answers `415` (wrong content type) or `400`
(not valid JSON).

request.description: Changes to the request sent to the backend.

response.description: Changes to the response sent to the client.

oneOf.description:
OpenID Connect login for browsers: authorization code flow with PKCE, a stateless
encrypted session cookie, claims to headers and to the consumer (F-GW-01).

algorithms.description:
ID-token algorithms accepted: those the provider advertises in
`id_token_signing_alg_values_supported` and that are listed here. HS256/384/512 use
the client secret as key and are accepted only when listed explicitly.

allow_private_targets.description:
Allow the provider's endpoints to resolve to private, loopback or link-local
addresses (an in-cluster Keycloak or Dex). Off by default.

allowed.description:
Who may log in. Everyone the provider authenticates when all lists are empty;
otherwise a user matching any one entry.

claims_to_headers.description:
Request headers set from ID-token claims (`claim: header`). Client-sent copies are
always removed first.

client_id.description: The client ID registered at the provider.

client_secret.description:
The client secret, as a `${file:…}`, `${env:…}` or `${vault:…}` reference. Without it
rdock is a public client and relies on PKCE alone.

consumer_claim.description:
The claim that becomes the request's consumer (rate limits, quotas, the cache key,
the access log). `sub` is used when the token lacks it, and in place of `email` when
the provider has not verified the address (`email_verified` is not `true`; see
`allowed.unverified_emails`).

forward_access_token.description:
Pass the access token to the backend in `X-Forwarded-Access-Token`. It is then kept
in the session cookie, which grows.

groups_claim.description: The claim that lists the user's groups (a string or an array of strings).

issuer.description:
The provider's issuer URL; its configuration is read from
`<issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration`. `https://` (or a loopback address).

logout_path.description:
Path that ends the session (`GET`, `HEAD` or `POST`, from the site itself: a request
another site triggers is refused with `403`); the provider's `end_session_endpoint` is
called when it advertises one (RP-initiated logout).

map_to_consumers.description:
Treat a consumer name that `consumers` defines as that consumer: the session then
gets its groups, and shares its quota, rate-limit and cache identity with its API keys
(other names stay keyed on the issuer). Off by default: an OIDC user is a separate
identity, keyed on the issuer and the name, so a user whose claim happens to equal a
configured consumer's name gains nothing from it. Turn it on only when the provider controls the
claim (it cannot be chosen by the user).

post_logout_path.description: Where the browser lands after logging out (a path on the same host).

redirect_path.description: Path of the callback the provider redirects back to. The route must match it.

redirect_url.description:
The full redirect URI registered at the provider, when it cannot be built from the
request (a route without a `Host` rule, a port the browser does not see). Its path
replaces `redirect_path`.

scopes.description:
Scopes requested; must include `openid`. Add `offline_access` where the provider needs
it for refresh tokens.

token_endpoint_auth.description: How the client authenticates at the token endpoint when it has a secret.

unauthenticated.description:
Requests without a valid session: `auto` redirects page navigations (`GET`/`HEAD`
asking for `text/html`) to the login and answers `401` to everything else, so API
and XHR clients never get a redirect; `redirect` always redirects `GET` and `HEAD`;
`deny` always answers `401`.

oneOf.description:
Count abuse signals (response statuses, failed authentications) per key in a window
and ban keys past a threshold for a while (H-SEC-01). Per instance; bans survive
restarts and binary upgrades.

action.description:
What a banned key gets: `deny` (`403`, problem type `banned`, the default), `tarpit`
(held for `tarpit.delay`, then denied) or `tag` (served; the access log and later
middlewares see `abuse: tagged`).

ban.description: How long a ban lasts. Default 10m.

events.description:
What counts: status codes (`401`), classes (`4xx`) and `auth_failure` (an
authentication middleware refused the credentials). Default `[401, 403]`.

exempt.description:
Client networks never counted or banned. Default the loopback networks; the
`security.trusted_proxies` networks are always added, so a proxy whose clients are not
resolved can never ban itself, and with it everyone behind it.

key.description:
What to count by: `client_ip` (the default; IPv6 by /64), `consumer`, `ja4` or
`header:<Name>`. Requests without a consumer or fingerprint count by client address.

max_bans.description:
Bans at once. The ban list is separate from the counters and nothing evicts a ban
before it ends: when it is full, new bans are refused and counted in
`rdock_abuse_bans_refused_total`. Default 10000.

max_keys.description: Keys counted at once; past it, the oldest counters are dropped. Default 100000.

threshold.description: Events within one `window` that start a ban. Default 20.

oneOf.description:
An adaptive concurrency limit (H-LB-04, ADR-0031): it learns how many requests the
routes using it can have in flight from their latency (`aimd` or `gradient`) and
answers the rest with `503` and `Retry-After`, routes of the lowest `priority_class`
first. Off unless configured.

backoff_percent.description: `aimd` only: the limit is multiplied by this percentage on a drop (default 90, 50–99).

initial.description: The limit at start and after a reload (default 20, Netflix's, kept within `min`–`max`).

interval.description:
`gradient` only: time between two measurements of the no-load latency (default 60s,
the `min_rtt_calc_params.interval` of Envoy's documented example; 1s–1h).

jitter_percent.description:
`gradient` only: a random part of `interval` added to it, in percent, so instances do
not measure at the same moment (default 15, Envoy's `jitter`; 0–100).

latency.description:
`aimd` only: a sample slower than this counts as a drop (default 5s, Netflix's
`timeout`). Measured from admission to the response headers.

probe.description:
`gradient` only: samples at `min` concurrency that make one measurement of the no-load
latency (default 50, Envoy's `request_count`; 5–1000).

queue.description:
`gradient` only: requests allowed above the estimate (default 4, Netflix's
`queueSize`).

shares.description: The share of the limit `normal` and `sheddable` routes may fill, in percent.

smoothing_percent.description: `gradient` only: the weight of a new estimate, in percent (default 20, 1–100).

tolerance_percent.description:
`gradient` only: how much slower than the no-load latency a sample may be before the
limit shrinks, in percent (default 150, Netflix's `rttTolerance` 1.5; 100–1000).

percent.description: Share of requests copied, from 1 to 100.

service.description: The service that receives the copies (`name` or `name@provider`).

alerts.description:
Where certificate alerts (renewal failures, near expiry) are sent besides the log,
the metrics and `rdock status`.

metering.description: Usage events per request with a consumer, for analytics and showback (F-GW-05).

domains.description: E-mail domains (the part after `@` of the verified `email` claim).

emails.description: E-mail addresses (the verified `email` claim), compared without case.

unverified_emails.description:
Also trust an `email` claim that comes without `email_verified` (some providers never
send it): for `emails` and `domains`, and as the consumer name when `consumer_claim`
is `email`. Unsafe with a provider that lets users set an address they do not own.
Off: only `email_verified: true` counts; `email_verified: false` never does.

OidcSameSite.description: The `SameSite` attribute of the session cookie.

oneOf.description: Sent on same-site requests and top-level navigations from other sites.

Sent only on same-site requests. Refused: the browser would not send it on the
redirect back from the provider, and the login would loop.
Sent on every request (needs `secure`).

allow_insecure_cookies.description: Explicit opt-in for `secure: false` (local development without TLS).

cookie_name.description:
Name of the cookie, without prefix. `__Host-` is prepended when `secure` is on and no
`domain` is set, `__Secure-` when `secure` is on with a `domain`.

domain.description: Share the cookie with subdomains of this domain. Host-only (and `__Host-`) when unset.

key.description:
The key that encrypts the cookie (at least 32 bytes), as a `${file:…}`, `${env:…}` or
`${vault:…}` reference. Every replica needs the same key. Use `keys` to rotate.

key_file.description: A file holding the key (read on every reload), instead of `key`.

keys.description: Keys for rotation: the first encrypts, all decrypt. References, as `key`.

refresh.description:
Use the refresh token, when the provider issues one, to renew the session before the
tokens expire; a failed refresh means a new login.

secure.description:
Send the cookie over HTTPS only. Turning it off is refused unless every route using
the middleware is plain HTTP and `allow_insecure_cookies` is set.

ttl.description:
Longest session, from login. Without a refresh token the session also ends when the
ID token expires.

OnNonJson.description: What `transform` does with a request body that is not JSON.

oneOf.description: Forward it unchanged.
Answer `415` or `400`.

OnPatchError.description: What `transform` does when a request patch cannot be applied.

oneOf.description: Answer `422` (problem type `patch-failed`).
Forward the body unchanged.

OnStale.description: What a GeoIP database older than `max_age` does.

oneOf.description: Log a warning and keep using it.
Refuse to load it.

OutlierDetection.description:
Outlier detectors (Envoy's outlier detection). Failures are those of passive health:
connection errors, resets, timeouts and `statuses`.

failure_percentage.description: Ejects a backend whose failures reach `threshold` percent of its requests.

interval.description: How often the detectors look at the counts of the last interval. Default 10s (Envoy).

success_rate.description: Ejects a backend whose success rate is below `mean − stdev_factor × σ` of the others.

PassiveHealth.description: Ejection of backends that keep failing.

ejection.description:
How long an ejected backend stays out before one request tries it again; doubled for
each ejection in a row, up to 5 minutes.

ejection_jitter.description:
Up to this much is added at random to each ejection time, so backends ejected by many
instances do not all return at once (Envoy's `max_ejection_time_jitter`). Default 0s.

failures.description: Failures within `window` that eject a backend.

max_ejection_percent.description: Largest share of the pool ejected at once, in percent.

outlier.description:
Statistical detectors that compare backends with each other once per interval and eject
the outliers through the same ejection as `failures` (back-off, `max_ejection_percent`,
trial request).

statuses.description: Answers that count as failures, besides connection errors, resets and timeouts.

oneOf.description:
Adds `value` at `path`: a new member, an array element inserted before the index (`-`
appends), or the whole document for `""`. The parent must exist.
Removes the value at `path`, which must exist.
Replaces the value at `path`, which must exist.
Removes the value at `from` and adds it at `path`. `path` must not be inside `from`.

from.description: Where the value is copied from.

oneOf.description:
Fails the patch unless the value at `path` equals `value` (numbers by their numeric
value, objects regardless of member order).

regex.description:
A regular expression for the whole path, with named groups (`(?<id>[^/]+)`). A path it
does not match fails validation.

schema.description: A schema for the object of the groups' values, converted like `query`.

PriorityClass.description: A route's class for load shedding by `admission` (H-LB-04).

oneOf.description: Shed last: may fill the whole limit.
The default: may fill `shares.normal` of the limit.
Shed first: may fill `shares.sheddable` of the limit.

file.description: More configuration files, merged with this one.

kubernetes.description: Kubernetes Gateway API and Ingress resources.

ProxyProtocolIn.description:
Inbound PROXY protocol settings (v1 and v2). A header is read only from `trusted` sources;
a connection from anywhere else that starts with a PROXY header is closed.

optional.description:
Also accept connections from `trusted` sources that send no header. Off by default: a
load balancer that stops sending headers would otherwise make every client look like
the load balancer itself to IP filters, rate limits and logs.

trusted.description:
Sources allowed to send a PROXY header, as IP addresses or CIDR networks. Others are
rejected when they send one.

oneOf.description: Text format.
Binary format.

QueryKey.description:
How the query string enters the key. Parameters left out of the key are also removed
from the request sent to the origin.

oneOf.description: The query exactly as forwarded.
Parameters sorted by name.
Only these parameters (`name` or `prefix*`).
All but these parameters (`name` or `prefix*`).

QuotaWindow.description: A quota's calendar window, in UTC.

oneOf.description: From the start of each hour.
From 00:00 UTC.
From 00:00 UTC on the 1st.

RateOverride.description: A limit for the consumers of one group.

period.description: Period of `average`; defaults to the middleware's.

RedirectPrefix.description: A path prefix replaced by another (`redirect.prefix`).

from.description:
The prefix to replace, starting with `/`. It matches whole path segments: `/a`
matches `/a` and `/a/x`, not `/ab`.

to.description: Its replacement, starting with `/`, or empty to remove the prefix.

oneOf.description: `http://`.
`https://`.

RedisStore.description:
A Redis-compatible server (Redis, Valkey, …) for cluster-scoped limits. rdock uses
`INCRBY`, `DECRBY`, `PEXPIREAT`, `ZADD`, `ZREMRANGEBYSCORE`, `ZCARD`, `TIME` (membership is
judged by the server's clock; without it, by each instance's), `AUTH`, `SELECT` and
`PING`.

allow_plaintext.description:
Allow `redis://` (no TLS) to an address that is not a loopback address. Off by default:
the password and the counters would cross the network in clear.

ca_file.description: CA certificates (PEM) to verify the server with instead of the system's roots.

key_prefix.description: Prefix of every key rdock writes. Default `rdock:`.

password.description:
The password. A secret: reference a file or a variable, e.g.
`"${file:/run/secrets/redis}"`.

timeout.description:
The longest a connection or a command may take before the store counts as away.
Default 1s (100ms–10s).

url.description:
`rediss://host:6379/0` (TLS) or `redis://host:6379/0`; the path is the database
number. Plain `redis://` is accepted for loopback addresses only, unless
`allow_plaintext` is set. Credentials belong in `username` and `password`, not here.

username.description: The ACL user name (Redis 6 and later); without it `AUTH` sends only the password.

oneOf.description: Apply them (RFC 9111 §5.2.1).
Ignore them, except `only-if-cached`.

Respond.description: A fixed answer of a service (`respond`): the status with ReverseDock's error page.

budget_percent.description:
Retries in flight may be at most this share of the requests in flight, in percent
(at least 3 are always allowed), so retries cannot overload a failing pool.

per_try_timeout.description:
Abandons an attempt that has not finished a read for this long and retries it on
another backend, within the budget and only where a retry is allowed (`on` must list
`timeout`). It replaces `timeouts.read` for every read of such an attempt, the wait for
the response headers and each pause of the response body; the last attempt and
requests that cannot be retried wait `timeouts.read`.

retry_non_idempotent.description: Also retry non-idempotent methods such as POST. Only safe if backends are idempotent.

RetryOn.description: Retryable failures. Nothing is retried once the client has received a response.

oneOf.description:
The connection to the backend could not be established (also a connect timeout).
Nothing reached the backend, so this is retried for every method.
The connection was reset before response headers arrived.
The backend did not answer within `timeouts.read`.
The backend answered `502 Bad Gateway`.
The backend answered `503 Service Unavailable`.
The backend answered `504 Gateway Timeout`.

insecure_unsigned.description:
Send updates without TSIG. Anyone who can reach the server could then change the zone, so
this is only for servers that authorize updates by address.

nameserver.description: IP address of the primary nameserver: `ip` (port 53), `ip:port` or `[ipv6]:port`.

tsig_key_name.description: Name of the TSIG key, as the server knows it.

tsig_secret.description:
The TSIG key's secret, base64 as `tsig-keygen` prints it. Write it as a `${file:…}` or
`${env:…}` reference.

zone.description:
The zone to update, such as `example.com`. Found with SOA queries to `nameserver` when
omitted.

Rollout.description: Staged rollout of published revisions (H-HA-02, ADR-0031).

auto_rollback.description:
Rolling back automatically when the canary's health drops: planned, only `false` is
accepted.

canary.description:
The instance that takes each revision first. When it is offline or not set, the first
online instance by name is chosen.

canary_timeout.description:
How long the canary has to report on a revision; without a report by then the rollout
halts. Default 2m (10s–1h).

mode.description:
`canary` (default) or `all`. The first revision of a cluster and rollbacks (including
an abandoned rollout) always go to every instance at once.

soak.description:
How long the canary serves a revision it acknowledged before the rest take it. Default
60s (0s–24h).

RolloutMode.description: How a revision is rolled out.

oneOf.description:
One canary takes the revision first; the rest follow after `soak` once it acknowledged
it. A refusal (NACK) by any instance halts the rollout.
Every connected data plane takes the revision at once.

Route.description: An HTTP route: which requests it matches, which middlewares run, which service answers.

enabled.description: Set to `false` to keep the route defined but inactive.

errors.description: How rdock renders its own error answers on this route, instead of `defaults.errors`.

listeners.description: Listeners the route is attached to. Defaults to `defaults.listeners`.

match.description: Requests this route handles: a Traefik v3 rule or a structured match.

max_body.description: Request body size for this route, instead of `security.limits.max_body_bytes`.

mirror.description: Send a copy of requests to another service and ignore its answers.

priority.description: Higher priorities are evaluated first. `0` uses the rule length, like Traefik.

priority_class.description:
Which requests an `admission` middleware sheds first under overload: `sheddable`,
then `normal` (the default), `critical` last. Unrelated to `priority`, which orders
matching.

service.description:
Service that handles matching requests (`name` or `name@provider`). Required unless the
last middleware answers every request itself (`static` without `pass_through`, or
`maintenance` enabled for everyone).

timeouts.description: Upstream timeouts for this route, overriding the service's.

tls.description: TLS for this route: `auto`, `off` or detailed settings. Defaults to `defaults.tls`.

Route53Provider.description: Amazon Route 53 (`type: route53`), in the standard AWS partition.

access_key_id.description:
Access key ID of the key pair. Read for every call like the secret, so both can rotate
together; a `${file:…}` or `${env:…}` reference or the ID itself.

api_url.description: For tests only: another API base URL, `http://` only on a loopback address.

hosted_zone_id.description:
The hosted zone ID, such as `Z0123456789ABCDEFGHIJ`; it may name a private zone. Public
zones are found by name when omitted; private zones are skipped.

region.description:
The AWS region of the deployment. Route 53 is global and signed as `us-east-1` in the
standard partition; the China and GovCloud partitions are not supported.

secret_access_key.description: Secret access key. Write it as a `${file:…}` or `${env:…}` reference.

session_token.description:
Session token of temporary (STS) credentials. Write it as a `${file:…}` or `${env:…}`
reference.

RouteTimeouts.description: Upstream timeouts of a route. Unset values come from the service.

RouteTlsOptions.description: Detailed TLS settings of a route.

certificate.description: A certificate from `certificates` to use instead of automatic issuance.

dns_provider.description: DNS provider (a key of `acme.dns_providers`) for DNS-01; required for wildcards.

domains.description: Names to put on the certificate instead of the route's hosts.

RuntimeSettings.description: The proxy's async runtime (ADR-0031). Read at start: a change takes effect after a restart.

max_blocking_threads.description:
Most threads for blocking work (file reads, DNS lookups by the system resolver).
Unset: 512, tokio's default.

worker_threads.description:
Threads that serve connections. Unset: one per CPU the process may use, tokio's
default.

oneOf.description: `Lax`.
`Strict`.
`None` (requires `secure`).
HTTP/1.1 in cleartext.
HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 over TLS.
HTTP/2 in cleartext (gRPC without TLS).

HTTP/3 over QUIC. Not supported in this version (planned, ADR-0032): Pingora 0.9 has no
QUIC connector.

vault.description:
A `HashiCorp` Vault or `OpenBao` server whose KV version 2 secrets secret fields may
reference as `${vault:<mount>/<path>#<field>}`.

Security.description: Client IP trust and request limits.

client_ip_header.description: Where the real client IP comes from.

trusted_proxies.description: Proxies whose forwarded headers are believed. Headers from anyone else are replaced.

Service.description:
An HTTP service: a pool of backends, a weighted split over other services, or a fixed
answer.

failover.description:
How traffic moves between backend `priority` tiers. `strict` (the default): a tier gets
traffic only when every tier above it has no available backend. `spill`: a tier keeps
`healthy share × overprovisioning` of the traffic (at most all of it) and the rest goes
to the next tier, as Envoy's priority levels do.

hedge.description:
Hedged requests: a second attempt while the first is still waiting. Planned, not
supported: Pingora 0.9 cannot race two upstream attempts of one request. Use
`retries.per_try_timeout` for stalled attempts.

load_balancer.description: How a backend is chosen for each request.

locality.description:
Prefer backends in the proxy's own zone (`locality` at the top level sets the zone).
Omitted, the top-level `locality.mode` applies.

max_connections_per_backend.description: Requests in flight to one backend; a backend at the limit gets no more until one ends.

max_requests.description: Requests in flight across the pool; more are answered `503` (circuit breaker).

overprovisioning.description:
With `failover: spill`: how much more than its share each tier can carry. Default 1.4
(Envoy's `overprovisioning_factor`): a tier keeps all traffic until fewer than about
71 % of its backends are available.

pass_host_header.description: Forward the client's `Host` header (otherwise the backend address is used).

respond.description:
Answer every request with this status instead of forwarding it, e.g. `500` for a
share of a split that has no valid backend. Set this, `backends` or `split`.

retries.description:
Retries of failed requests (ADR-0010, ADR-0015, ADR-0022). Without this setting the
defaults below apply: a connection that cannot be opened is tried again on another
backend, up to twice, within the retry budget (ADR-0028). `attempts: 0` turns retries off.

scheme.description: Protocol spoken to the backends. gRPC uses `h2c` (cleartext) or `https`.

split.description:
Weighted traffic split over other services (canary, blue/green). Set this, `backends`
or `respond`.

tls.description: TLS to the backends when `scheme` is `https`.

ServiceLocality.description: The locality preference of one service.

SessionLimit.description: A number of sessions (at least 1), or `unlimited`.

SetCookie.description: What to do with responses that set a cookie.

oneOf.description: Never store them.
Store them without `Set-Cookie`.

SlowStart.description: Time to full weight, such as `30s`, or every setting.

SlowStartConfig.description:
Slow start, every setting (Envoy's `SlowStartConfig`): the weight is
`weight × max(min_weight_percent / 100, (elapsed / window)^(1 / aggression))`.

aggression.description: Shape of the ramp: 1.0 (the default) is linear; above 1 ramps faster at first.

min_weight_percent.description: The weight starts at this share, in percent. Default 10 (Envoy).

on.description:
When a backend ramps: `recovery` (after failed probes or an ejection; the default) and
`join` (a backend that newly appears in a pool that already had a backend at full
weight; never at start-up or into an empty pool).

SlowStartOn.description: When a backend's weight ramps up.

oneOf.description: After recovering from failed probes or an ejection.
When it newly appears in a pool that already had a backend at full weight.

SmtpTls.description: How the SMTP connection is protected.

oneOf.description: Plain connection upgraded with STARTTLS (port 587).
TLS from the first byte (port 465).
No encryption; refused unless the host is a loopback address.

SpiffeRules.description:
SPIFFE X.509-SVID checks on a client certificate (SPIFFE standards `X509-SVID.md` and
`SPIFFE-ID.md`, commit 5d15e3ee of github.com/spiffe/spiffe, 2026-11-13): exactly one URI
SAN, scheme `spiffe`, a valid trust domain and a non-root path, a leaf that is not a CA and
may not sign certificates or CRLs. The chain itself is verified by the listener's
`client_auth`, whose CA bundle must be the trust domain's.

Make the SPIFFE ID the request's consumer (for `rate_limit` and `quota` by consumer,
metering and the access log). Its issuer is `spiffe://<trust domain>`, so it never
shares counters with an API-key or token consumer of the same name. Off by default.

id_prefixes.description:
SPIFFE ID prefixes, matched segment by segment: `spiffe://prod.example.com/ns/web`
accepts that ID and every ID below it, never `/ns/webshop`. With neither `ids` nor
`id_prefixes`, any ID of the trust domains is accepted.

SplitTarget.description: One target of a weighted split.

StartTls.description: Protocols whose own request to start TLS a `tcp` listener answers.

oneOf.description:
PostgreSQL: answer the 8-byte `SSLRequest` with `S` (and a `GSSENCRequest` with `N`),
so clients with the default `sslnegotiation=postgres` reach TCP routes that read SNI.

StaticCacheControl.description: `Cache-Control` of static files: a default and overrides by path prefix.

default.description: Value for files no prefix matches. `no-cache` makes clients revalidate with the `ETag`.

max_age.description: Lifetime; a session cookie when omitted.

previous_secrets.description: Keys of earlier rotations: cookies signed with them stay valid and are replaced.

secret.description:
Key that signs the cookie, as a `${file:…}` or `${env:…}` reference. Without it, a key is
generated once and kept in `$RDOCK_DATA_DIR/sticky.key`.

StructuredMatch.description: Structured match conditions. All given conditions must hold.

client_ips.description: Any of these client IPs or CIDR ranges.

headers.description: Header name → exact value; all must match.

query.description: Query parameter → exact value; all must match.

SuccessRateDetector.description: The success-rate detector, with Envoy's defaults.

minimum_hosts.description:
Backends with enough requests needed before anything is evaluated. Default 5; at
least 3.

request_volume.description: Requests in the interval for a backend to count. Default 100.

stdev_factor.description: Multiplier of the standard deviation. Default 1.9 (Envoy's 1900 / 1000).

oneOf.description: Each running task directly; ReverseDock balances, health-checks and drains them.

The service's virtual IP; Swarm balances between tasks. Active health checks and
sticky sessions have nothing to act on and are ignored.

endpoint.description: Docker Engine API endpoint of a manager node.

endpoint_mode.description: Route to each running task (the default) or to the service's virtual IP.

expose_by_default.description: Expose services without `rdock.enable=true`. Off by default.

network.description: Overlay network used to reach services.

poll_interval.description:
How often services and tasks are listed. Swarm sends no events when a task starts or
stops, so this bounds how long a new or stopping task waits to join or leave its pool.
At least `1s`.

static_roots.description:
Directories on ReverseDock's file system that `static` middlewares from service labels
may serve (`rdock.static.root`). Empty, the default, refuses every such middleware, so a
service cannot read ReverseDock's own files (ADR-0027).

oneOf.description: None: a path with a symbolic link in it answers `404`.
Links that stay inside `root`; the kernel refuses any resolution that leaves it.
Every link, also out of `root`. `rdock validate` warns about it.
One datagram per record.
A stream with octet-counted framing.
The same stream over TLS, with the server's certificate and name verified.

delay.description: How long a request is held before the `403`. Default 5s, at most 60s.

max_held.description:
Requests held at once, all keys together; past it, banned requests are denied at once
(holding connections costs the proxy too: HAProxy's manual warns that a tarpit "can
make things worse"). Default 100.

TCP keep-alive on accepted connections (`SO_KEEPALIVE`). Unset values keep the kernel's
(Linux: 7200 s idle, 75 s between probes, 9 probes).

listeners.description: Listeners (`tcp` or `https`) the route is attached to.

Middlewares checked before connecting to the service: `ip_allow`, `ip_deny` and
`in_flight` (counted per client IP).

TLS handling. Without it the bytes are relayed as they arrive; with it the route
matches TLS connections only and terminates TLS unless `passthrough` is set.
