proxy_protocol.description: Send a PROXY protocol header to backends.

connect.description: Establishing a connection to a backend.

idle.description:
A connection with no data in either direction for this long is closed (NGINX
`proxy_timeout`).

termination_delay.description:
Once one side has finished sending, the other side gets this long to finish too
before both are closed (Traefik `terminationDelay`).

allow_critical.description:
Let the tenant's routes use `priority_class: critical` with an `admission` middleware
it does not own (a shared one). Off: critical traffic on a shared limit is the
administrator's to define.

backend_networks.description:
Networks the tenant's backends may connect to. Empty: globally routable unicast
addresses only (no loopback, link-local, private, unique-local, shared, multicast,
documentation, reserved or cloud metadata address), checked on IP literals at
validation and on every address a DNS name or SRV record resolves to, each time it
resolves. Set: exactly these networks (a cloud metadata address only when listed on
its own), and backends must be IP literals.

dashboard.description: Planned: a dashboard view limited to the tenant.

hosts.description:
The host names the tenant's routes may match: `shop.example.com` or
`*.shop.example.com` (any name below it, not the name itself). Claims of two tenants
may not overlap.

limits.description:
Ceilings on what the tenant's objects may hold, so one tenant cannot use up what
tenants share (disk, the ACME account's rate limits).

metrics_label.description: Planned: a `tenant` label on the core metrics.

prefix.description:
The start of the names of the tenant's objects in the admin API (routes, services,
middlewares). Defaults to `<tenant>-`. No tenant's prefix may start another's.

shared.description:
Objects outside the prefix that the tenant's objects may reference (`name` for the
configuration file's, `name@provider` for a provider's).

TenantLimits.description:
Ceilings on a tenant's objects. The defaults are small on purpose; an administrator raises
them per tenant.

max_body.description:
The largest request body a tenant route accepts, and the most its `hold_body`,
`transform` and `validate` middlewares may hold (default 16MiB). A tenant route without
`max_body` gets this one, or `security.limits.max_body_bytes` when that is smaller.

max_tls_names.description:
Distinct host names the tenant's routes may get automatic certificates for (default
20): each one is an order on the ACME account every tenant shares, and Let's Encrypt
limits certificates per registered domain and orders per account.

TenantShared.description: Objects outside a tenant's prefix that its objects may reference.

connect_attempt.description:
Establishing a connection when a failed connect would be retried on another
backend: the attempt gives up after this long, so a stopped backend costs about a
second instead of `connect` (ADR-0026). The last attempt always waits `connect`.

TlsFingerprint.description:
Which TLS client fingerprints an `https` listener computes, and whether backends see them.
The values are computed from the outer ClientHello (with Encrypted Client Hello the inner
one is never seen), only for connections this listener terminates.

header.description:
A request header that carries the JA4 value to the backend, e.g. `X-JA4`. A copy sent
by the client is always removed. Unset (the default): backends do not see it.

ja3.description:
JA3 (Salesforce, an MD5 of the ClientHello). Off by default: legacy, since Chrome 110
randomises the extension order that JA3 hashes, one browser has many JA3 values.

ja3_header.description: A request header that carries the JA3 value (needs `ja3: true`).

ja4.description: JA4 (FoxIO, BSD 3-Clause). Default on when `fingerprint` is set.

TlsMode.description: `auto` issues certificates automatically; `off` serves the route without TLS.

oneOf.description: Automatic certificates (ACME) for the route's hosts.
No TLS.
TLS 1.3 only.
TLS 1.2 and 1.3 with forward-secret AEAD ciphers (Mozilla "intermediate").

TlsSessionCache.description: The in-memory session cache of a TLS listener.

size.description: Sessions kept (0 turns the cache off). Default 256, rustls's default.

TlsTickets.description:
TLS session tickets. A ticket lets a returning client skip the full handshake. Listeners
share ticket keys only when their TLS policy, client authentication (mode and CA
certificates), certificate scope and these settings are equal, so a session from a listener
without client authentication can never be resumed on one that requires it. 0-RTT (early
data) is never accepted.

key_file.description:
Keys you provide, to share tickets between instances: one or more 32-byte keys in base64,
one per line (`openssl rand -base64 32`), the first current, the others still accepted.
The file must not be readable by the group or others, is read again when it changes, and
rotating it is then your job (a warning when it is older than 24 hours). Without it, keys
are generated, live in memory only and are handed to the next process in a binary
upgrade.

rotate.description:
How often a new ticket key is made; the previous key still decrypts for one more
interval, so tickets live at most twice this (announced to clients, capped at 7 days by
RFC 8446 §4.6.1). Default 6h, rustls's own default; at most 84h.

TokenEndpointAuth.description: Token endpoint client authentication (OpenID Connect Core §9).

oneOf.description: HTTP Basic with the client ID and secret.
The client ID and secret in the form body.

TokenSource.description: Where a JWT is read from. The first one present wins: header, cookie, query parameter.

header.description: A header; `Authorization` values must start with `Bearer `.

query.description: A query parameter (tokens in URLs end up in logs; prefer a header).

sample_ratio.description: Share of requests traced, from 0 to 1.

headers.description: Header operations, applied in the order remove, set, add (as `headers` does).

TrustedProxy.description: `cloudflare` (edge ranges synced automatically) or an IP address/CIDR range.

oneOf.description: HMAC-SHA256, the one RFC 8945 recommends.
HMAC-SHA384.
HMAC-SHA512.
HMAC-SHA1: accepted with a warning; RFC 8945 does not recommend it.
HMAC-MD5: refused by validation; RFC 8945 says it must not be used.

UdpHealth.description: Health of the backends of a UDP service.

passive.description:
Ejection after ICMP "port unreachable" answers (seen as refused sends or receives on a
session's connected socket). On by default.

tcp_check.description:
Periodic TCP connection probes, for backends that also listen on TCP (a DNS server
does on port 53). Off by default: a generic UDP probe cannot tell a healthy server
from one that drops datagrams.

when_all_down.description: What happens when no backend is healthy.

UdpLbPolicy.description: How a UDP session's backend is chosen.

oneOf.description: Weighted round-robin.
Weighted random.
Fewest open sessions relative to the weight.

Consistent hash of the client IP: every session of a client goes to the same backend
while it is up.

UdpLoadBalancer.description: Backend selection for new UDP sessions.

UdpPassiveHealth.description: Passive health of a UDP service.

ejection.description:
How long an ejected backend gets no new sessions before one session tries it again;
doubled for each ejection in a row, up to 5 minutes.

enabled.description: Count refusals and eject backends. `false` only ends the affected session.

failures.description: Refusals within `window` that eject a backend.

max_ejection_percent.description: Largest share of the pool ejected at once, in percent.

UdpRoute.description:
A UDP route: the datagrams of its `udp` listeners go to its UDP service. The backend is
chosen once per session (a client address and port) and kept for the session's life.

enabled.description: Set to `false` to keep the route defined but inactive.

listeners.description: `udp` listeners the route is attached to (required).

match.description:
Rule made of ``ClientIP(`…`)`` matchers only (with `&&`, `||`, `!`). Omitted, the route
takes every datagram of its listeners; a listener has at most one such route.

middlewares.description:
Middlewares checked before a session is created: `ip_allow` and `ip_deny`. A datagram
they refuse is dropped without an answer.

priority.description: Higher priorities are evaluated first. `0` uses the rule length.

UdpService.description:
A UDP service: backends that receive the datagrams of UDP routes. Each session (one client
address and port) gets its own connected socket to one backend, chosen when the session
starts.

backends.description:
Backend servers (`host:port`; Unix sockets are not supported). `weight` sets each
one's share of new sessions; `backup` ones get sessions only when no other is up.

health.description: Backend health: passive ejection on ICMP "port unreachable", optional TCP probes.

load_balancer.description: How a new session's backend is chosen.

requests.description:
Detach a session from its client address after this many datagrams from the client
(NGINX `proxy_requests`): the next datagram opens a new session, possibly to another
backend, while the detached one still relays its replies until `responses` or `idle`
ends it. `1` balances every datagram on its own.

responses.description:
End a session after this many datagrams from the backend (NGINX `proxy_responses`).
`1` suits request-and-answer protocols such as DNS: the socket is released as soon as
the answer is relayed. Omitted, a session ends only when idle.

UdpSessions.description:
Session caps of a `udp` listener. Both are on by default: a UDP source address can be
forged, so without a cap anyone could make the listener open sockets until it runs out of
file descriptors (each session holds one socket and one task). Datagrams that would open
a session over a cap are dropped and counted in `rdock_udp_dropped_total`, never answered.

max.description:
Sessions of the whole listener. Default 4096: Envoy caps UDP sessions per cluster at
1,024 by default (`max_connections` circuit breaker, checked 2026-11-11 in
docs/research/v0.8-cache-extensibility.md §5.1); a listener here stands for a cluster
and may serve several clients' DNS bursts, and 4,096 sockets stay far below the
container default of 1,048,576 open files. `unlimited` removes the cap.

max_per_client.description:
Sessions per client IP address (any source port). Default 64, so one source (or one
forged address) can take at most 1/64 of the listener's default budget; a resolver
that forwards many parallel queries from one address may need more. `unlimited`
removes the cap.

UdpTcpCheck.description: TCP probes of the backends of a UDP service.

healthy.description: Consecutive successes before a backend is healthy.

port.description: TCP port to connect to; the backend's port when omitted.

unhealthy.description: Consecutive failures before a backend is unhealthy.

idle.description:
A session with no datagram in either direction for this long is closed and its socket
released. Default 60 s, Envoy's `udp_proxy` default; Traefik uses 3 s and NGINX
10 minutes (sources in docs/research/v0.8-cache-extensibility.md §5.1, checked
2026-11-11).

Unauthenticated.description: What `oidc` does with a request that has no valid session.

oneOf.description: Redirect page navigations to the login; `401` for everything else.
Redirect every `GET` and `HEAD` to the login; `401` for other methods.
Always `401`.

UnknownOperations.description: What `validate` does with requests outside the OpenAPI document.

oneOf.description: Answer `404` (no path template matches) or `405` (the path exists, the method not).
Let them through unchecked.

Upgrade.description:
In-place binary upgrades (H-PERF-04, ADR-0031): `rdock upgrade` on the admin Unix socket or
`SIGUSR2` hands the listeners to a new process, which serves once it is ready; this one
drains and exits. Linux only; refused when rdock is PID 1 (replace the container instead).

binary.description:
The binary `SIGUSR2` and `rdock upgrade` without `--binary` run. Default
`/usr/local/bin/rdock`, where the systemd unit and the release image install it. It
must be a regular file owned by root or rdock's user and not writable by the group or
others, in a directory with the same owners that the group and others cannot write to
(unless it is sticky, like /tmp).

drain.description:
How long the old process may still serve its open connections (HTTP/1 keep-alive is
switched off and HTTP/2 clients get GOAWAY at once); the rest are closed then. Default
10m (Envoy's drain time); `unlimited` waits for every connection, which keeps an old,
possibly vulnerable binary serving for as long as a client holds a connection.

start_timeout.description:
How long the new process may take to report that it is ready, and then that it serves;
otherwise the old process resumes and the upgrade fails. Default 30s.

trusted_keys.description:
minisign public keys (`RWQ…`); when set, `<binary>.minisig` must be a valid signature of
the binary by one of them.

ca_file.description: CA bundle used instead of the system roots.

server_name.description: SNI and verification name, when it differs from the backend host.

verify.description: Verify the backend certificate and host name.

oneOf.description: Refuse invalid requests.
Log and count invalid requests, and let them through.

VaultAuth.description: How rdock logs in to Vault.

oneOf.description:
A token, as a `${file:…}` or `${env:…}` reference (read again on every request, so a
token file rotated by an agent is picked up).

Kubernetes service-account login (`POST /v1/auth/<mount>/login`); the token is renewed
by logging in again before its lease runs out.

VaultSettings.description:
A Vault or `OpenBao` server (`secrets.vault`).

Values are read when a configuration is loaded and every `refresh`; a changed value reloads
the configuration. They stay in memory only: the configuration, its history, snapshots, the
admin API, logs and diagnostics keep the `${vault:…}` reference.

address.description:
The server, e.g. `https://vault.internal:8200`. `https://` only, or `http://` to a
loopback address (a dev server or a local agent), unless `insecure_http` is set.

allow_private_targets.description:
Allow a server on a private address (`10.0.0.0/8`, …). On by default: Vault usually
runs inside the network.

ca_file.description: CA certificates (PEM) that sign the server's certificate, instead of the system's.

insecure_http.description:
Allow `http://` to a server that is not on a loopback address. **Unsafe**: the token
and every secret cross the network unencrypted. Validation warns.

namespace.description: A Vault Enterprise or `OpenBao` namespace, sent as `X-Vault-Namespace`.

refresh.description: How often referenced values are read again.

timeout.description: Time allowed for one request to the server.

WasmCapability.description: A host interface a WASM plugin may be granted.

oneOf.description: `rdock:plugin/log`: write lines to rdock's log (32 per request, 1 KiB each).
`rdock:plugin/clock`: read the wall clock.
`rdock:plugin/random`: read random bits from the operating system.

Webhook.description: An HTTPS endpoint that receives JSON events.

token.description: Bearer token sent in `Authorization`. Write it as a `${file:…}` or `${env:…}` reference.

WhenAllDown.description: Behaviour when every backend is unhealthy.

oneOf.description: Send to every backend anyway: a broken health check must not cause an outage.
Answer `503`.
